items.heading: Start From the Lane, Then
items.text: Start from the lane, then work back to the stream. If the lane you want needs Biology, you need PCB or PCMB. If it needs Maths, you need PCM or PCMB. Check the step before you pick the stream.

items.heading: Be Strict Before Choosing Pcb
items.text: Be strict before choosing PCB. Choose it only with real interest in biology and health or life-science work, an honest view of the long training and the seat competition, enough family runway, and a written backup lane. Respect for the doctor title is not a reason.

items.heading: Pcm Is the Broader Default
items.text: PCM is the broader default only for an undecided student who can sustain maths. It keeps technology, data and many degrees open, while closing medicine, dentistry, veterinary and some agriculture and life-science routes. A student who cannot realistically carry the maths load should not choose it.

items.heading: Write a Second Route, Whatever
items.text: Write a second route, whatever you choose. Every lane marked Not so scalable needs a skill beside it that can earn and grow on its own.

items.heading: "Science Is the Safe Stream
items.text: "Science is the safe stream." Science gives range, not a result. Several well-known science routes are crowded and slow to pay.

items.heading: "Respected Means Scalable
items.text: "Respected means scalable." We rate each lane on how far skills, proof and a business layer can grow income, not on prestige.
